Computer vision: $103 billion in 2025 — how visual analysis is transforming customer relationships

⏱ 5 min read📅 November 5, 2026✍️ custovox.ai

The global Computer Vision market reaches $103.13 billion in 2025, up +$55 billion since 2020. The path to $233 billion by 2032 confirms that visual analysis will become a standard enterprise AI dimension. But where does this technology create value for customer service teams today?

From industrial quality control to customer experience

Historically, Computer Vision developed in industrial contexts: quality control, security surveillance, facial recognition. But since 2022-2023, new use cases emerge in customer relationships: automatic analysis of customer-submitted photos, product defect classification from returns, visual evaluation of hospitality or restaurant conditions.

Customer photos: an untapped data source

Every day, thousands of customers send photos through customer service channels. These photos arrive in email inboxes, complaint forms, ticket systems — and remain systematically unanalyzed in the vast majority of companies. A Computer Vision tool can automatically classify these photos and trigger appropriate alerts in seconds.

The three most impacted sectors

Hospitality and restaurants: room photos, dish photos, common area photos — every negative photo is a potential improvement signal.

Retail and e-commerce: damaged packaging, defective product photos — automatically identifiable to prioritize returns and prevent negative reviews.

Industry and construction: defect photos, site issues — archivable and searchable by visual similarity.

Physical AI integrates Computer Vision

According to Deloitte, 21% of global AI leaders identify intelligent security systems as having the greatest impact among physical AI types. These systems rely on Computer Vision. Their adoption will accelerate between 2025 and 2030, driven by falling sensor and vision model costs.

What this means for you

custovox.ai's VisualIQ automatically analyzes photos sent by your customers — returns, hospitality, restaurants, retail. Automatic classification, real-time alerts, report in 48h.
